reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents Forsage as a participation and business opportunity, asks viewers to activate with $155, recruit webinar attendees, register, and share with friends, while claiming an immediate $155 transfer as 100% income and citing monthly returns. The visible dashboard and supplied directions provide related context, but they do not verify that transfers occurred, that the stated returns were realized, or that the platform's full terms were disclosed.

opening.argument: The speaker does not present this as risk-free or ask viewers to accept a verdict without understanding it: he says he experienced losses after not getting into the subject, and urges viewers not to judge without full knowledge. That caveat supports reading the presentation as an invitation to investigate a new subject, not proof that a return is assured. His account of the program includes claims that need independent checking, but these excerpts do not establish that he concealed uncertainty or guaranteed every viewer a profit.

citations.quote: I had some losses because I didn't get into it.
Without getting the full knowledge, it is not right to judge.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution emphasizes activation, recruitment, and a claimed transfer, but those statements alone do not establish that the transfer occurred or that every participant was promised a realized return. Its own account concedes that the supplied material does not verify transfers or returns. The speaker's caution to understand the subject before judging is relevant context: the presentation may be making a disputed business case, not certifying an outcome.

citations.quote: Without getting the full knowledge, it is not right to judge.
if the program activates using $ 155, then immediately we will be transferred $ 155 to you

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The caution is about learning before judging, not a warning that viewers could lose money by joining. The presentation then instructs viewers to invite people and describes activation with $155 followed by a transfer to the promoter. The earlier reference to past losses does not qualify those participation claims or show that viewers were told the promised payment was uncertain.

opening.argument: The presentation devotes substantial attention to explaining blockchain, cryptocurrency, and how transactions and wallets work. The speaker explicitly introduces the subject as blockchain education and walks through concepts before showing a platform interface. A dashboard demonstration and an explanation of a proposed program can be educational content even when the speaker also expresses a favorable view of participation. The excerpts do not independently establish that the educational claims are false or that the material is only a solicitation.

citations.quote: We are going to discuss about Blockchain as the future.
The next level of Internet in which we look is Blockchain.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the material education does not account for its concrete enrollment pitch. The video moves from general blockchain discussion to a $155 activation, inviting a list of prospective participants, and describing a payment to the promoter when the program activates. Those are not merely explanations of blockchain technology; they show that the instructional framing is being used to present participation as an opportunity.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The educational opening does not change the purpose of the later platform walkthrough: viewers are shown how the matrix entries relate to activation and recruiting participants, and are urged to register. The presenter describes an immediate $155 transfer tied to another person's activation, while the closing speaker promotes registration and monthly returns. That is a participation pitch embedded in an educational presentation, not a detached technology lesson.

opening.argument: The material can be read as promoting an online affiliate business and explaining its payment and account mechanics, rather than demonstrating that money was taken through deception. It discusses cryptocurrency, wallets, exchange transactions, and a platform dashboard; the sampled dashboard shows an account interface, not proof of a completed payment or a loss. The supplied excerpts do not show a request for passwords or other credentials, nor do they verify the meaning or basis of the displayed figures. A promotional referral arrangement may be questionable, but these materials alone do not establish that the underlying service is fraudulent.

citations.quote: You can use this app as your mobile phone, It is called Affiliate Marketing.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's strongest evidence is not simply that the video shows a dashboard: it is the spoken connection between recruited participants, paid activation, and a transfer to the promoter. Even if the displayed figures do not verify a completed payment, the video's own pitch describes income linked to participants joining. That makes ordinary-commerce framing incomplete.

citations.quote: if the program activates using $ 155, then immediately we will be transferred $ 155 to you
3 people for the project

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The presentation itself supplies the missing connection: it asks viewers to invite prospective participants, describes activation using $155, and says the promoter will then receive $155. It also lays out matrix entries and says later entries depend on further participation. Calling this affiliate marketing or showing a dashboard does not make those recruitment-linked payments ordinary retail sales, and the video provides no independent verification that the claimed income is sustainable or realized.
